paragraphs.text: An oolong from Nantou, in Taiwan, made in 2024. [GABA oolong](gaba:definition) names a way of making tea rather than a plant or a place. The method was found in Japan in 1987, and Taiwan's tea research station [adapted it to oolong](gaba:history), after which it spread among the island's makers.

For hours before it is made in the usual way for [Taiwan oolong](taiwan-oolong:definition), the fresh leaf is kept [without oxygen](gaba:making), in a sealed chamber filled with nitrogen or drawn to a vacuum. With no air, the leaf turns its glutamic acid into GABA and cannot break it down again, so the amino acid builds up. Taiwan's method alternates rounds without oxygen with rounds in air instead of one long spell.
At two years this is a young tea. Taiwan's [lao cha](taiwan-oolong:ageing) tradition keeps well roasted oolong for years, and those who name a figure count an oolong as old only after ten to thirty.

brewing.text: In a cup or pot, steep it for about two to five minutes. It is forgiving of small changes in water temperature and steeping time. It can also be cold-brewed, steeped for some hours in the fridge.

notice.text: Ripe, dried or stewed fruit such as apricot, honeyed sweetness, a smooth, round body, and little bitterness or astringency; often brown sugar or roasted grain, sometimes wood or spice, and a light fruity sourness.
